{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — FX Platform License Agreement (Customer-Side Review)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Licensor's draft License Agreement

## Executive summary

The draft is materially one-sided in the Licensor's favour and, as drafted, sits at or beyond our playbook walk-away thresholds in several places. The three critical items are risk allocation and ownership: there is no Licensor indemnity at all (Article XII runs only from us, and Article XIII(a) expressly excludes Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims); Article XIII caps only Licensor's liability, at one half of fees paid, with no carve-outs, while our liability is unlimited; and Article III plus the "Derivative Work" definition give Licensor ownership of the bespoke front end and enhancements we commission and pay for under Article VII(b), with no provision confirming that our trading, order and client data remain ours.

A second cluster concerns control and exit. Licensor holds a unilateral option to extend the 36-month Initial Period by seven years, with no non-renewal mechanism and no cap on fee increases, while we have no termination-for-convenience right at all. Licensor may terminate immediately on any Licensee breach with no materiality threshold or cure period, and Article XX(a) terminates our licenses on any Change of Control of Licensee unless Licensor consents — an effective veto over our own M&A. There is no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation on a hosted platform where our records sit on Licensor's systems, and no affirmative performance warranty (Article VIX is a pure "AS IS" disclaimer). Lower-priority gaps are audit procedure, a one-way three-year non-solicit, and the absence of any vendor insurance covenant.

Four rules are already compliant and require no redline: exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete and governing law (New York law with exclusive New York state and federal jurisdiction, no arbitration provision). One rule, MFN, could not be completed and needs manual review.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XII; Art. XIII(a)–(b)) | Add a Licensor defence and indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with standard notice/control/cooperation, disapply the Article XIII limitations to it, and narrow our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our own breach of applicable law. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions (with Art. III, ¶0048; definitions ¶0005, ¶0008) | Insert customer-side carve-outs after ¶0048: assignment of custom deliverables we pay for (with licence-back of embedded Licensor IP), retention of all rights in our data, and no joint ownership. Licensor's pre-existing platform IP is preserved. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XIII) | Make the consequential-damages exclusion and the cap mutual, reset the cap to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, add uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and confirm fee obligations are not damages for cap purposes. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions (with Art. XX(a)) | Add an affiliate/successor carve-out for Licensee, make consent mutual and subject to a reasonableness standard, bar Licensor assignment to our competitors, and delete the change-of-control termination/consent/re-pricing right. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions (Art. II(II)(c), (e); Art. IV) | Extend the grant to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (we remain responsible for compliance), confirm transferability to a successor, and limit termination to material breach uncured after 30 days' notice. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II License Grant and Restrictions (Arts. IV, XIX–XXI) | Add a Licensee right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirm Licensor has no mid-term convenience exit. Fallback: 60–90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § II License Grant and Restrictions | Grant is non-exclusive both ways; no sole-supplier or requirements covenant. No redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation | No LDs, penalty or early-termination fee payable by us; Art. XXIII bars termination damages against either party. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § I Certain Definitions | Restrictions on us are scope-of-licence/IP-protection limits only; no restraint on our business or on using competing platforms. No redline. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Art. II §IV(b) (fee tiers, "50+ US$5.00") | Cap audits at once per 12 months, with 30 days' prior written notice, during business hours, a confidentiality-bound auditor, and no access to our systems or facilities. Existing 5% cost-shifting threshold is acceptable and left as-is. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. X(b)) | Narrow the one-way Term-plus-three-years restriction to a mutual 12-month restriction covering only personnel directly involved in performance, retaining the existing general-advertising and unsolicited-inquiry carve-out. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions (Art. IV) | Replace Licensor's unilateral seven-year extension option with mutual written 12-month renewals, 60 days' notice of renewal and any fee change, and an uplift cap at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Fallback: 12-month auto-renewal with 30-day (max 60-day) opt-out and 5% cap. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Missing | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XXI) | Insert new Article XXI(c): up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Licensee Data in machine-readable form within 30 days, and deletion with written certification. Fallback: 90 days. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Missing | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX) | Add an express warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformance of the Licensed Software to the Documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy, carved out of the "AS IS" disclaimer. Fallback: 90 days / 30 days. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions (¶¶0145–0146) | New York law, exclusive jurisdiction of New York state and federal courts; no arbitration provision. No redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § II License Grant and Restrictions (Art. V) | Fees are usage-based tiers plus the USD 2,500/month support fee; no committed floor, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic. Volume rebate runs in our favour. No redline. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Needs review | — | Automated review failed (tool loop exceeded 12 iterations). Requires manual review. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | General Provisions (new subsection (l) after ¶0159) | Insert a Licensor insurance covenant: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Licensor touches our data, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. Binds the counterparty only. |

## Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as at or beyond our walk-away thresholds and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **No Licensor indemnity plus a broad one-way Licensee indemnity**, compounded by the Article XIII(a) exclusion of Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims (INDEMN).
2. **Liability cap of one half of fees paid, benefiting Licensor only**, below the six-month floor, with unlimited Licensee liability and no carve-outs (LOL-CAP).
3. **Licensor's unilateral seven-year renewal option**, with no Licensee consent right and no cap on fee increases (RENEWAL).
4. **One-way non-solicit for the Term plus three years covering all Licensor and Affiliate personnel**, beyond the 24-month/all-personnel threshold (NOSOLICIT).
5. **Pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no affirmative performance warranty** (WARRANTY).
6. **Silence on transition assistance and data return** on a hosted platform holding our trade and account records (TRANSITION).
7. **Assignment and change-of-control provisions** — no affiliate/successor carve-out, no reasonableness standard, and Licensor consent effectively a veto over our own M&A under Article XX(a) (ASSIGN).

We would also treat the IP position (Licensor ownership of bespoke deliverables we pay for, and no confirmation that our data is ours) as a must-fix given its criticality.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline reflecting the proposals above, prioritising the three critical items (INDEMN, IP, LOL-CAP) and the exit cluster (RENEWAL, T4C, ASSIGN, TRANSITION) in the cover note.
2. Complete the manual MFN review before we send; we do not want to close on pricing terms with that rule unresolved.
3. Confirm with the business the operational inputs we need to hold the line: expected 12-month fee run-rate (to size the LOL-CAP figure), which Affiliates and contractors need platform access (LICENSE), and the realistic migration window off the platform (TRANSITION — six months preferred, 90 days as fallback).
4. Confirm with the deal team whether any near-term corporate transaction is contemplated, which would elevate ASSIGN and the Article XX(a) change-of-control trigger to a gating issue.
5. Note for the negotiation record that EXCLUSIVITY, LD, NONCOMPETE, GOVLAW and MINCOMMIT are already compliant, so we should resist any Licensor trade that reopens them.
"}
